issues.legal_issue: A High Court exercising rent-control revisional jurisdiction cannot set aside concurrent findings of fact merely because it reappraises the evidence and considers another view possible.
material_facts: The Rent Controller and the Appellate Authority both found that the landlord had a bona fide requirement of the premises.
The High Court reappraised the evidence and reached a different factual conclusion, without identifying a basis showing that the concurrent findings were illegal or perverse.
The matter reached the Supreme Court in an appeal challenging the High Court’s exercise of revisional jurisdiction.
issues.conclusion: The High Court exceeded its revisional jurisdiction. Its judgment was set aside, and the Rent Controller’s order as upheld by the Appellate Authority was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Revisional jurisdiction under rent-control legislation is narrower than appellate jurisdiction and cannot be used as an appeal in disguise or to rehear factual issues. Under Hindustan Petroleum Corporation Ltd. v. Dilbahar Singh, relying on Sri Raja Lakshmi Dyeing Works and Dattonpan, a High Court may correct findings that are perverse, unsupported by evidence, reached without considering material evidence, based on misreading of evidence, grossly erroneous, or otherwise not according to law; it may not reappraise evidence merely to reach a different factual view.

rule.if: rent_control_revision and concurrent_factual_findings and high_court_reappraised_evidence and different_view_only and not identified_factual_illegality

predicates.rent_control_revision: The proceeding is a revision concerning a decision made in a rent-control matter.
predicates.concurrent_factual_findings: The original decision-maker and the first appellate decision-maker reached the same factual finding.
predicates.high_court_reappraised_evidence: The High Court reconsidered the evidence when exercising revisional jurisdiction.
predicates.different_view_only: The High Court displaced the factual finding because it considered another view of the evidence possible.
predicates.identified_factual_illegality: The High Court identified that the factual finding was affected by a legal error, perversity, or another defect that made it not according to law.

issues.definition: When a rent-control revision involves concurrent factual findings and the High Court reappraises evidence to adopt a different view without identifying a defect that makes those findings unlawful, those findings must not be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant operating a hotel business may be granted time to surrender possession after an eviction order is restored, subject to conditions protecting the premises and the landlord’s interest.
material_facts: The respondent sought time to surrender vacant possession after the Supreme Court restored the eviction order.
The respondent was carrying on a hotel business in the premises.

The Court allowed the respondent to remain temporarily, required surrender of vacant and peaceful possession by the specified deadline, prohibited creation of third-party rights and damage to the property, and required an undertaking.
issues.conclusion: The respondent was permitted to remain in the premises temporarily, subject to surrendering possession by the specified deadline and complying with the stated safeguards.
issues.legal_principle: Having regard to the respondent’s hotel business, the Court exercised its discretion to allow temporary continuation in the premises while requiring an undertaking and safeguards against third-party rights and damage; no earlier case or statutory provision was cited for this direction.

predicates.eviction_order_restored: The court restored an order requiring the tenant to give up possession of the premises.
predicates.tenant_requested_time: The tenant asked the court for additional time before surrendering possession.
predicates.tenant_operates_hotel_business: The tenant was carrying on a hotel business in the premises.

issues.definition: When an eviction order is restored, the tenant has requested time, and the tenant operates a hotel business in the premises, the tenant may receive conditional time to surrender possession.
